text: Firebrand is a name used by several characters in American comic books published by DC Comics. Rod Reilly, the first Firebrand, appeared in Police Comics #1 through #13 from August 1941 to November 1942, published by Quality Comics; he was the bored and wealthy son of a steel tycoon who fought crime with his servant and friend, "Slugger" Dunn. Originally drawn by Reed Crandall, Rod wore a transparent shirt and red pants with a bandana mask covering the top half of his face, and he used a lariat and could climb buildings with vacuum cups. After DC acquired Quality Comics, Firebrand was largely inactive until the mid-1970s when he joined the Freedom Fighters. He was killed in a fight with the Silver Ghost in a photocopied issue of Cancelled Comic Cavalcade, which was never released and thus it is uncertain if this event is part of the current DC Universe. When DC collected characters into the All-Star Squadron, it was retconned that Rod had been injured in a surprise attack and replaced by his sister, Danette Reilly. In All-Star Squadron #5 (1981), Danette discovers Rod's identity while staying at his penthouse and muses on his relationship with Slugger Dunn, wondering why a bachelor playboy would need a bodyguard, and finds a hidden closet that makes her realize she didn't know her brother as well as she thought. Danette, a volcanologist, was first introduced in a special "All-Star Squadron" preview in Justice League of America #193 (August 1981), where she was studying volcanoes north of Hawaii when kidnapped by time-traveling villain Per Degaton and sorcerer Wotan. During her escape, Wotan hit her with a magical blast and hurled her into a pit of lava; the combination of magic and lava gave her the ability to control heat and project fire blasts. Her powers emerged after she put on Rod's costume, and since Rod was injured in the attack, she decided to become the new Firebrand. Because Degaton returned to the future after being defeated, the All-Star Squadron forgot the attack. Danette was initially racist toward the Japanese, but after visiting her brother in the hospital, he revealed he had been saved by a soldier whose parents were Japanese, who later died from his wounds, and she realized her prejudice and began showing more respect to people of Japanese descent. Danette appeared in Crisis on Infinite Earths, where she briefly reunited with her former lover, the reluctant supervillain Cyclotron, who, though deceased, phased into her time to assist her and assumed partial custody of his daughter Terri alongside the Atom. In Stars and S.T.R.I.P.E. (2000), Firebrand was revealed to have been killed by the Dragon King; she has remained dead since. During the Absolute Power event (2024), Firebrand's spirit was found in the Well of Souls in Themyscira and was used as a power source by the Amazo android Paradise Lost. Her name is a tribute to creator Roy Thomas' wife, Danette Thomas. The Quality Comics character Wildfire was originally intended to play a major role in All-Star Squadron, but DC objected due to her name being shared with a Legion of Super-Heroes member, so Danette Reilly was introduced instead. Firebrand was ranked 67th in Comics Buyer's Guide's "100 Sexiest Women in Comics" list. In February 1996, DC introduced a third Firebrand, former police detective Alejandro "Alex" Sanchez. After nearly dying in an explosion that destroyed his apartment, Sanchez underwent experimental surgery to restore mobility, paid for by philanthropist Noah Hightower, who later offered him advanced armor combined with implants to give him enhanced strength and speed for up to four hours. After his partner was attacked, Sanchez agreed to become Firebrand, and his armor emitted green flame, giving him a demonic appearance. Sanchez's storyline reflected concerns about racial injustice and violence against people of color. His tenure lasted only nine issues in his self-titled comic, and he reappears in JSA: Secret Files #2, where he is killed by a Checkmate knight in Roulette's arena. In April 2006, Andre Twist was introduced in The Battle for Blüdhaven after being exposed to Chemo, gaining control over fire; he also appears in Uncle Sam and the Freedom Fighters as a member of the new Freedom Fighters, carrying a bo staff and possessing athletic and martial arts skills. In the 2007 Freedom Fighters series, Firebrand develops a relationship with Red Bee and is devastated when she is taken over by an alien insectoid race; together, the Freedom Fighters save Red Bee and repel the invasion. In the 2010 Freedom Fighters series, Firebrand is killed by Charles Lane, the grandson of the Jester. The fifth Firebrand, Janet Fals, appeared in The Unexpected, released in June 2018. Janet was killed during the Dark Multiverse invasion, but her father used his CIA connections to bring her back to life, releasing her remains to Civil Solutions, a futurist arms developer, who resurrected her with a new heart called the "Conflict Engine," which requires her to start fights to stay alive, preventing her from returning to her old life or identity. She quenches her needs by fighting in underground matches as Firebrand. She had a flirtation with Joy, a female receptionist at V.A. Hospital in Mammoth City, and her creator Steve Orlando has confirmed she is a lesbian. Rod Reilly's Firebrand had no true super-powers but was personally trained by ex-heavyweight boxer "Slugger" Dunn to achieve physical perfection.
